Find local maxima in a binned genomic signal

Source: R/peaks.R
find_rt_peaks.Rd

Within each chromosome, bins are split into blocks at gaps between consecutive starts larger than max_gap (default: 1.5 times the median bin step). Runs of equal scores (within plateau_tol) form plateaus. A plateau of at most max_plateau_bins bins is a peak if it has at least max(1, ceiling(flank_bins / 2)) non-NA bins among the flank_bins bins on each side, is higher than all of them by more than plateau_tol, is at least min_score (unless NULL) and exceeds the median of the flanking bins by at least min_delta. The middle bin of the plateau is reported.

Usage

find_rt_peaks(
  granges,
  score_col = "score",
  flank_bins = 5,
  min_score = 0.2,
  min_delta = 0.02,
  max_plateau_bins = 5,
  max_gap = NULL,
  plateau_tol = 1e-08
)

Arguments

granges

GRanges of bins with a numeric score column (e.g. from calculate_pseudobulk_rt()).

score_col

Name of the score metadata column.

flank_bins

Positive integer; flank size on each side.

min_score

NULL or the minimum peak score. We use 0.2 on RT scores and 10 on track-centre counts.

min_delta

Minimum difference between the peak and the flank median.

max_plateau_bins

Maximum plateau size.

max_gap

NULL or the maximum start-to-start distance within a block.

plateau_tol

Tolerance for equal scores.

Value

A sorted GRanges of peak bins with additional metadata columns RT_value (the score), local_median, local_delta and plateau_size.
